verified: Hub Registry verifies exact completed assignment projection and result digest without issuing or promoting identities
Hub-only registered-source resolution revalidates immutable source bindings; Worker consumers retain explicitly pinned lookup
Scoped SQL source reads verify tenant/project and admitted byte digest
Model-input admission verifies actual Tool RUN completion, exact result, request origin, immutable admitted bytes, current source policy, revision, environment, assignment and chat revision
Output SRC pins must have the exact Tool result origin, content digest and policy; unrelated registered identities are refused
Repeated runs, failed runs, altered text, unknown identities, stale source/chat revisions, paused chat and corrupted SQL/Registry bytes are rejected
remaining: Implement Hub model-run reservation before actual execution over admitted model request and verified tool sources
Bind exact model result to its reserved assignment and lease; preserve current control checkpoints
Wire assigned dialog/toolbox and execution ports into installed runtime; combined normal Task acceptance
architecture_review: A focused model-input verifier depends on a read-only admitted-content port and the existing policy/Registry ports (SRP/DIP/ISP). SQL content persistence and Hub identity verification remain separate. Existing global policy/service locator coupling remains; inject those ports in the model controller rather than reading repositories from the Worker. The caller must obtain and revalidate current assignment authority around admission and execution; this verifier alone does not grant execution.
scope_boundaries: Actual HTTP Tool admission, SQL source/Registry stores and identity verification use explicit synthetic Task/MCP/index/policy fixtures
Two negative cases deliberately corrupt SQL rows; the other-domain source is genuinely issued by the test Hub Registry, not self-assigned
No model request is executed or reserved by this new verifier, and no grounded model-answer or production-release claim is made
